To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a factor of 3–6 improvement in ALROC was obtained with the Vision over the mCT for lesions 10 mm in diameter and larger, with smaller lesions being barely detected in the Flow, and that this improvement was reduced when postreconstruction smoothing was applied.

the improved physical performance of the Biograph Vision PET/CT leads to a factor of 6 reduction in imaging times or injected dose for lesions at least about 10 mm in diameter and that the improved spatial resolution also leads to improved measured contrast and, thus, better quantification of lesion uptake.

the improved performance provided by the latest digital whole-body scanners results in a factor of 2–3 reduction in imaging time or injected dose for lesions at least about 10 mm in diameter and that this reduction in dose or time can be increased to 4–6 times for smaller, high-uptakes lesions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new generation of PET scanners that are capable of providing a significant improvement in lesion detectability, leading to shorter imaging times or lower injected doses.
the development and evaluation of novel imaging and image analysis methods to improve the detection and characterization of cancer.
the impact of improved performance on clinical performance and the potential for reduced imaging times or injected doses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Vision provides a 3–6-fold reduction in imaging time over the mCT, depending on lesion size and uptake.
improved physical performance of the Vision results in a factor of 3–4 improvement in detectability for small lesions and a factor of 6–7 improvement for larger lesions.
the improved performance leads to a significant improvement in detectability for all lesions studied, but the benefit of improved performance is reduced by the use of postreconstruction smoothing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a factor of 3–4 reduction in imaging time is possible with the Vision over the mCT flow, with the caveat that the Vision is better able to quantify the uptake.
improved physical performance leads to improved clinical performance.
the latest-generation digital PET scanners provide a substantial improvement in clinical performance, allowing for a substantial decrease in imaging time or injected dose.
The main takeaway from our work is that

improved performance of the new generation of PET/CT systems can be used to improve the clinical performance in terms of lesion detectability, leading to reduced imaging times and lower injected dose.
improved PET performance leads to improved clinical performance, allowing shorter acquisition times or lower injected dose.
the Vision’s improved spatial resolution and time-of-flight performance leads to better lesion detectability and quantification.
